items.stem: (a) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the path of a ray of light incident obliquely on one face of a glass slab. (b) Calculate the refractive index of the material of a glass. Given that the speed of light through the glass slab is 2 × 10⁸ m/s and in air is 3 × 10⁸ m/s. (c) Calculate the focal length of a lens, if its power is −2.5 D.
items.answer:
(a) The ray diagram shows the incident ray striking the first face obliquely, bending towards the normal inside the slab, emerging from the opposite face parallel to the incident ray and laterally displaced from it.
(b) Speed of light in glass slab, v = 2 × 10⁸ m/s; speed of light in air, c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
n = c/v = (3 × 10⁸)/(2 × 10⁸) = 1.5
Hence, refractive index of material of glass slab is 1.5.
(c) Power, P = −2.5 D; focal length, f = ?
P = 1/f
f = 1/P = 1/(−2.5) = 100 cm/(−2.5) = −40 cm = −0.4 m
The focal length of a lens of power −2.5 D is −0.4 m or −40 cm.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode; MinerU printed the exponent of the glass speed as $2 \times 10^{s}$ — restored to 2 × 10⁸ m/s from the worked solution (n = 3×10⁸/2×10⁸ = 1.5). The solution also mislabels f as 'Total length' — read as focal length. A stray fragment (f = −20 cm, h_o = 4 cm, v = −10 cm) printed just after this answer belongs to an earlier question's solution and was not used.

items.stem: "A lens can form a magnified erect image as well as magnified inverted image of an object placed in front of it." State the nature of this lens and draw ray diagrams to justify the above statement. Mark the positions of O, F and 2F in the diagram.
items.answer:
The lens is a convex (converging) lens — a convex lens is used to form a magnified erect image as well as a magnified inverted image of an object.
Magnified and erect image: when the object is placed between the optical centre O and the focus F (within the focal length), the image formed is virtual, erect and magnified, on the same side of the lens as the object.
Magnified and inverted image: when the object is placed between F and 2F, the image formed is real, inverted and magnified, beyond 2F on the other side of the lens.
In both ray diagrams the positions of O, F and 2F are marked on the principal axis.
items.ocr: Curly quotes in the printed stem normalised to straight quotes. The printed answer consists of the two ray diagrams with the captions 'Magnified and erect image' and 'Magnified and Inverted Image'; the object positions were read from those diagrams.

items.stem: The image formed by a spherical mirror is real, inverted and is of magnification −2. If the image is at a distance of 30 cm from the mirror, where is the object placed? Find the focal length of the mirror. List two characteristics of the image formed if the object is moved 10 cm towards the mirror.
items.answer:
Given, m = −2, v = −30 cm, u = ?
m = −v/u
−2 = −(−30)/u
u = −30/2 = −15 cm
The object is at 15 cm in front of the mirror.
By using the mirror formula,
1/v + 1/u = 1/f
−1/30 − 1/15 = 1/f
(−1 − 2)/30 = −3/30 = −1/10 = 1/f
f = −10 cm
The focal length is 10 cm (concave mirror).
If the object is moved 10 cm towards the mirror it lies 5 cm from the pole, i.e. within the focus, so the image will be (i) virtual and erect and (ii) enlarged in size.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode. The printed mirror-formula step is OCR-damaged as '(−15 − 30)/40 = −45/450 = −1/10'; the arithmetic was restored as (−1 − 2)/30 = −1/10, which gives the printed f = −10 cm. 'v_0 = −30 cm' read as v = −30 cm.

items.stem: A mirror is fitted in a wall of the AGRA FORT. When you stand at a proper location, a full-size image of the Taj Mahal can be seen in this mirror. (a) What kind of mirror is it? (b) Draw a ray diagram for such a mirror when the object is at infinity.
items.answer:
(a) The mirror is a convex mirror.
(b) For a convex mirror with the object at infinity, the rays coming parallel to the principal axis appear to diverge from the principal focus F behind the mirror. The image is formed at the focus behind the mirror and is virtual, erect and highly diminished (point-sized).
items.ocr: The printed answer gives only 'The mirror is a convex mirror' plus the ray diagram; the description of the image at infinity was read from that diagram.

items.stem: An object is kept in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image is three times the size of the object. Calculate two possible distances of the object from the mirror.
items.answer:
Given, f = −20 cm.
For a real image, m = −3:
−3 = −v/u  ⇒  v = 3u
1/v + 1/u = 1/f
1/(3u) + 1/u = 1/(−20)
4/(3u) = −1/20
3u = −80  ⇒  u = −80/3 = −26.6 cm
For a virtual image, m = +3:
+3 = −v/u  ⇒  v = −3u
1/v + 1/u = 1/f
1/(−3u) + 1/u = 1/(−20)
2/(3u) = 1/(−20)
u = −40/3 = −13.33 cm
So the two possible object distances are 26.6 cm and 13.33 cm from the mirror.
items.ocr: The printed stem reads 'The image is three times the image of the object' — read as 'three times the size of the object', which is what the solution computes. The first branch of the worked solution is badly OCR-damaged (fragments '30i = −90', 'u = −266 cre'); it was restored to u = −80/3 = −26.6 cm, consistent with the legible second branch u = −40/3 = −13.33 cm.

items.stem: (a) Name the mirror that (i) can give real as well as virtual image of an object. (ii) will always give virtual image of same size of an object. (iii) will always give virtual and diminished image of an object. (iv) is used by a doctor for examining teeth. (b) With the help of a ray diagram explain the use of concave mirror as solar concentrators.
items.answer:
(a) (i) concave mirror, (ii) plane mirror, (iii) convex mirror, (iv) concave mirror.
(b) The solar concentrators are placed at the focus of a large concave mirror which focuses the Sun's heat rays on the concentrators, and a high temperature is achieved. A ray coming parallel to the principal axis will pass through the focus after reflection, so all the parallel heat rays from the Sun are concentrated at the focus where the concentrator is kept.
items.ocr: Printed stem shows '(iv) s used by a doctor' — leading 'i' lost by OCR, restored to 'is used'. Printed answer shows 'ocus' for 'focus'.

items.stem: (i) Under what conditions, a concave mirror produces a virtual and magnified image? Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the formation of image in the above case. Also state the position of object to produce magnified and real images. (ii) A ray of light moving along principal axis is falling on a concave mirror. Draw the path of reflected ray. Also state the values of angles of incidence and reflection in this case.
items.answer:
(i) When an object lies between the focus and the pole of the mirror, i.e. within the focus of a concave mirror, it produces a virtual and magnified image (formed behind the mirror). The image formed will be real and magnified when the object is placed between F and C of the concave mirror.
(ii) A ray of light travelling along the principal axis strikes the concave mirror normally (along the normal at the pole), so it is reflected straight back along the same path. Angle of incidence, ∠i = 0° and angle of reflection, ∠r = 0°.
items.ocr: Two-column bleed: the answer to part (ii) ('Angle of incidence ∠i = 0°, Angle of reflection ∠r = 0°' with its diagram) prints on page 46, far from the question; it was matched back to this question by content. The printed line 'between P and F' for the real-and-magnified case was read as between F and C, which is what the accompanying diagram shows.

items.stem: (a) Name the type of mirror used by a dentist to examine the teeth of a patient. (b) Name the type of mirror used as a rear-view mirror in motor cars. (c) Draw ray diagrams to show the image formation in both the above cases. Also state the position and nature of the image so formed.
items.answer:
(a) Concave mirror.
(b) Convex mirror.
(c) For the dentist's concave mirror (tooth held within the focus): the image is virtual, erect and magnified and forms behind the mirror.
For the rear-view convex mirror: the image is virtual, erect and diminished and forms between the pole and the focus behind the mirror.
items.ocr: None beyond stripping the page furniture; the two figures are worked-solution ray diagrams so no image is attached.

items.stem: Draw a ray diagram to show a virtual image of 2/5th the size of an object 4 cm high, using a spherical mirror. Mark the position of the object, image and focal length.
items.answer:
Given, h_o = 4 cm, h_i = (2/5) × 4 = 1.6 cm.
Since the image is virtual, erect and diminished (smaller than the object) for every object position, the mirror is a convex mirror.
In the ray diagram, PF = focal length, PA = object distance and PA′ = image distance. The 1.6 cm tall virtual, erect image is formed between the pole P and the focus F behind the mirror.
items.ocr: LaTeX '\frac{2}{5}th' rewritten as 2/5th. The printed 'Given' list repeats 'PA = Image distance' — the second entry is PA′ (image distance) and was corrected.

items.stem: For what position of the object does a concave mirror form a real, inverted and diminished image of the object? Draw a ray diagram.
items.answer: When the object is placed beyond C, i.e. beyond the centre of curvature of the concave mirror, the image formed is real, inverted and diminished, and it lies between the focus F and the centre of curvature C. The ray diagram shows one ray parallel to the principal axis reflected through F and one ray through F reflected parallel to the principal axis, meeting between F and C.
items.ocr: The board tag 'Delhi 2011' prints after the answer text; the printed answer text is only 'When the object is placed beyond C' plus a ray diagram, so the image description was read from that diagram.

items.stem: Draw a ray diagram in each of the following cases to show the position and nature of image formed when the object is placed (i) between pole and focus of a concave mirror. (ii) between focus and centre of curvature of a concave mirror. (iii) at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. (iv) between infinity and pole of a convex mirror. (v) at infinity from a convex mirror.
items.answer:
(i) Object between P and F of a concave mirror: image behind the mirror — virtual, erect and magnified.
(ii) Object between F and C of a concave mirror: image beyond C — real, inverted and magnified.
(iii) Object at C of a concave mirror: image at C — real, inverted and of the same size as the object.
(iv) Object between infinity and P of a convex mirror: image between P and F behind the mirror — virtual, erect and diminished.
(v) Object at infinity from a convex mirror: image at the focus F behind the mirror — virtual, erect and highly diminished (point-sized).
items.ocr: The printed answer is diagrams only — five ray diagrams labelled (i)–(v), with the (i) and (iv) labels lost by OCR. The position and nature of the image in each case were read off those diagrams and written out as the answer text.

items.stem: State the types of mirrors required to get (i) virtual and diminished image of an object. (ii) real and inverted image of an object. Show image formation in both the above cases in the form of ray diagrams. Which of the above mirrors can also form (i) real and magnified (ii) virtual and magnified image, of the object? Draw ray diagrams to justify your answer.
items.answer:
(i) Convex mirror — for every position of the object it forms a virtual, erect and diminished image between the pole and the focus behind the mirror.
(ii) Concave mirror — for an object beyond the focus it forms a real and inverted image in front of the mirror.
The mirror that can also form a real and magnified image of the object is the concave mirror; this can happen if the object is placed between C and F of the concave mirror.
A concave mirror can also give a virtual and magnified image of an object if the object is placed between F and P of the mirror.
items.ocr: No board/year tag is printed for this question. Two-column bleed: the closing part of this answer ('the mirror that can also orm real and magnified image…' and 'a concave mirror can also give a virtual and magnified image…') prints back on page 42 above the question; it was matched to this question by content, and 'orm' read as 'form'.

items.stem: (a) Draw a ray diagram in each of the following cases to show the position and nature of the image formed when the object is placed; (i) between optical centre and principal focus (F) of a convex lens. (ii) between F and 2F of a convex lens. (iii) at 2F of a convex lens. (b) How will the nature and position of image formed change in cases (i) and (ii) in part (a) of this question if the lens is replaced by a concave lens? Draw the corresponding ray diagram.
items.answer:
(a) (i) Object between O and F of a convex lens: image on the same side as the object — virtual, erect and magnified.
(ii) Object between F and 2F: image beyond 2F on the other side — real, inverted and magnified.
(iii) Object at 2F: image at 2F on the other side — real, inverted and of the same size as the object.
(b) If the convex lens is replaced by a concave lens, the image is virtual and erect in both the cases; it is diminished and is formed between the optical centre and the focus, on the same side of the lens as the object.
items.ocr: The printed answer for part (b) is only 'Virtual and erect in both the cases' plus a ray diagram; the diminished size and position were read from that diagram. Part (a) is diagrams only, described from them.

items.stem: A thin converging lens forms a; (i) real magnified image. (ii) virtual magnified image of an object placed in front of it. (a) Write the positions of the objects in each case. (b) Draw labelled ray diagrams to show the image formation in each case. (c) How will the following be affected on cutting this lens into two halves along the principal axis? (i) Focal length, (ii) Intensity of the image formed by half lens.
items.answer:
(a) (i) Between F and 2F of the lens. (ii) Within the focal length.
(b) Ray diagrams: for the object between F and 2F, the image is real, inverted and magnified beyond 2F; for the object within the focal length, the image is virtual, erect and magnified on the same side of the lens as the object.
(c) (i) There would be no effect on the focal length of the lens. (ii) Intensity would be reduced (the half lens gathers less light).
items.ocr: Two-column bleed: the answer to part (c) and the second ray diagram (captioned 'Within the focal length') print on page 47; they were matched back to this question by content.

items.stem: An object of 4.0 cm size is placed at a distance of 25 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. At what distance from the mirror should a screen be placed to obtain a sharp image of the object? Find the nature and size of the image formed.
items.answer:
Given, u = −25 cm, f = −15 cm, h_o = 4 cm.
Using the mirror formula,
1/f = 1/v + 1/u
1/v = 1/f − 1/u
Putting the values of u and f,
1/v = −1/15 + 1/25 = (−5 + 3)/75 = −2/75
v = −75/2 = −37.5 cm
The screen should be placed 37.5 cm in front of the mirror (on the same side as the object).
Nature of the image: real and inverted.
m = −v/u = h_i/h_o
−(−37.5)/(−25) = h_i/4
h_i = −6 cm
So the image is real, inverted and magnified, of size 6 cm.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode. The printed step reads '1/v = −1/15 + 1/2' — the 5 of 25 was lost by OCR; restored to +1/25, which gives the printed −2/75. The printed result line writes 'u = −75/2' where v is meant. The printed answer says 'Nature of the image Real or' — the word after 'Real' is cut off; taken as real and inverted, consistent with h_i = −6 cm.

items.stem: (a) Draw ray diagrams to show the formation of virtual image in case of the following mirror (i) concave mirror (ii) convex mirror (b) How can concave mirror help in harnessing Sun's energy?
items.answer:
(a) (i) Concave mirror: with the object placed between the pole P and the focus F (within the focus), the reflected rays diverge and appear to come from behind the mirror, giving a virtual, erect and magnified image.
(ii) Convex mirror: for any position of the object the reflected rays diverge and appear to come from a point between P and F behind the mirror, giving a virtual, erect and diminished image.
(b) Concave mirrors are used in solar furnaces to generate electricity. Principle: It works on the principle that when the rays of light fall parallel to the principal axis, after reflection from the concave mirror they meet at one point which is the focus of the mirror. The whole of the energy gets concentrated at that point and can be used as an alternative source of energy.
items.ocr: Part (a) of the printed answer is two ray diagrams with no text; the descriptions were read from those diagrams.

items.stem: (a) State the laws of refraction. (b) What is meant by the term absolute refractive index? The speed of light in a transparent medium is 0.6 times that of the speed in vacuum. Find refractive index of the medium. (c) How should a ray of light be incident on a rectangular glass slab so that it comes out from the opposite side of the slab without being displaced? Draw a ray diagram to illustrate your answer.
items.answer:
(a) The following are the laws of refraction of light:
(i) The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of two transparent media at the point of incidence, all lie in the same plane.
(ii) The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant, for the light of a given colour and for the given pair of media. This law is also known as Snell's law of refraction. If i is the angle of incidence and r is the angle of refraction, then sin i / sin r = constant. This constant value is called the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first.
(b) (i) The absolute refractive index of a medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in the medium.
(ii) The speed of light in vacuum = c; the speed of light in the medium = 0.6c
n = (speed of light in vacuum)/(speed of light in the medium) = c/(0.6c) = 1.66
(c) The ray of light should be incident normally (perpendicularly, at an angle of incidence of 0°) to the surface of the glass slab. It then passes straight through the slab without bending and emerges from the opposite side along the same line, with no lateral displacement.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode. Two-column bleed: the refractive-index arithmetic (c/0.6c = 1.66) and the answer to part (c) print on page 44, above question 208; they were matched back to this question by content.

items.stem: (a) State two characteristics of image formed by a convex mirror. (b) With the help of a diagram, define (i) pole, (ii) focal length of a concave mirror. (c) Convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles. Give reason.
items.answer:
(a) The image formed by a convex mirror is (i) virtual and erect and (ii) diminished.
(b) Pole: Pole of the mirror is the geometrical centre of the mirror (marked P in the diagram).
Focal length: Focal length (f) is the distance between the principal focus and the pole of the mirror.
(c) The image formed by a convex mirror is highly diminished. It can therefore give a wider field of view of the traffic behind.
items.ocr: Printed answer reads 'the principal focus arid the pole' — 'arid' corrected to 'and'. The printed (a) is just 'Erect and diminished'; expanded to the two characteristics asked for. The printed '(c)' label lost its opening bracket.

items.stem: (a) Draw ray diagrams for the following and state the nature, size and position of the image formed in each case (i) For a concave mirror, object at 2F. (ii) For a concave mirror, object between F and P. (iii) For a convex mirror, object between P and infinity. (b) Write the mathematical expression for magnification produced by mirrors. When do we say magnification produced is −1?
items.answer:
(a) (i) Concave mirror, object at 2F (i.e. at the centre of curvature): Nature of image — real and inverted. Size of image — same size as that of the object. Position of image — at 2F.
(ii) Concave mirror, object between F and P: Nature of image — virtual and erect. Size of image — magnified. Position of image — behind the mirror.
(iii) Convex mirror, object between P and infinity: Nature of image — virtual and erect. Size of image — diminished. Position of image — between P and F behind the mirror.
(b) m = h_i/h_o or m = −v/u.
Magnification produced is −1 when the image formed is of the same size as the object but real and inverted.
items.ocr: The printed answer lists only two labelled cases: '(i)' (real, inverted, same size, at 2F) and '(ii)' (virtual, erect, diminished, between P and F behind the mirror). The second of those describes the CONVEX mirror, i.e. part (iii) of the question — the concave 'object between F and P' case is missing from the print/OCR. It has been restored here as virtual, erect and magnified, and the convex description kept as (iii). Printed F′ read as F.

items.stem: Name the types of mirror(s) that should be used (i) as a rear-view mirror (ii) by the dentists. Also draw ray diagram(s) and mention the reason(s) for their use.
items.answer:
(i) Convex mirror, (ii) Concave mirror.
Reasons:
(i) A convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror as it always gives an erect and diminished image, and thus covers a large area of the traffic behind the vehicle.
(ii) When an object (tooth) is placed close to a concave mirror, i.e. within its focus, its erect and magnified image is formed, which makes it convenient for a dentist to examine teeth.
items.ocr: The printed answer labels the two halves '(a)' and '(b)' although the question uses (i) and (ii); relabelled to match the question. The second ray diagram for the dentist's concave mirror is not present in the OCR.

items.stem:
A student focused the image of a candle flame on a white screen by placing the flame at various distances from a convex lens. He noted his observation in the following table
Distance of the flame from lens (cm)Distance of the screen from lens (cm)
6020
4024
3030
2440
1270
Analyse the above table and answer the following questions: (i) What is the focal length of convex lens? (ii) Which set of observation is incorrect and why? (iii) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formation for any correct set of observation.
items.answer:
(i) For u = −60 cm, v = 20 cm, using 1/f = 1/v − 1/u:
1/f = 1/20 + 1/60 = (3 + 1)/60 = 4/60 = 1/15
f = 15 cm
Focal length of the convex lens = 15 cm.
(ii) The set u = 12 cm and v = 70 cm is incorrect, as in all the other sets we get f = 15 cm by using the given values of u and v, but in this set the value of f is different.
(iii) Ray diagram for the third set, where u = 30 cm and v = 30 cm: the object is at 2F, so the image is real, inverted and of the same size, formed at 2F on the other side of the lens.
items.ocr: HTML table kept verbatim from the source. Printed stem reads 'by placing the lame at various distances' — restored to 'flame'. In the worked solution the line 'f = 1/15 = 15 cos' was read as f = 15 cm.

items.stem: A student focused the image of a candle flame on a white screen using a convex lens. He noted down the position of the candle, screen and the lens as under (i) Position of candle = 12.6 cm (ii) Position of convex lens = 51.8 cm (iii) Position of screen = 91.0 cm (a) Calculate the focal length of the lens. (b) Where will the image be formed if he shifts the candle towards the lens at a position of 32.2 cm? (c) What will be the nature of the image formed if he further shifts the candle towards the lens? (d) Draw a ray diagram to show the formation of the image in case (c) as said above.
items.answer:
(a) Object distance, u = 51.8 − 12.6 = 39.2 cm and image distance, v = 91.0 − 51.8 = 39.2 cm.
Since u = v = 2f = 39.2 cm,
f = 39.2/2 = 19.6 cm
(b) With the candle at 32.2 cm, u = 51.8 − 32.2 = 19.6 cm, which equals the focal length, so the object is at the focus and the image is formed at infinity.
(c) If the candle is shifted still closer, it lies within the focal length, so the image is virtual and erect (and magnified), on the same side of the lens as the candle.
(d) The ray diagram shows the object between O and F of the convex lens with the refracted rays diverging and appearing to meet behind the object, giving an enlarged virtual erect image.
items.ocr: This question lost its printed number; it sits between question 210 and question 212 on page 47, so it is numbered 211 by position. The printed worked solution for (a) lists 'f = 39.2/2 = 19.6 cm' before the u and v lines (order scrambled by the column layout); it was reordered. Printed answers for (b) and (c) are the bare phrases 'At infinity' and 'Virtual and erect.'

items.stem: (a) Define 1 dioptre power of lens. (b) A 2 cm long pin is placed at a distance of 16 cm from a convex lens of focal length 12 cm. Find the position, size and nature of the image formed.
items.answer:
(a) One dioptre is the power of a lens of focal length one metre.
(b) Given, u = −16 cm, f = +12 cm, h_o = 2 cm.
Lens formula,
1/v − 1/u = 1/f
1/v = 1/f + 1/u
v = fu/(f + u) = (12 × (−16))/(12 + (−16)) = (−192)/(−4) = 48 cm
m = h_i/h_o = v/u = 48/(−16) = −3
h_i = m × h_o = −3 × 2 = −6 cm
So a real, inverted and magnified image of size 6 cm is formed at 48 cm from the lens, on the side opposite to the pin.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode. A stray worked fragment ('Using, P = 1/f; −2.0 D = 1/f(m); f = −0.5 m') prints inside this answer; it matches neither part (a) nor part (b) and is a column bleed from another question's solution, so it was not carried into the answer. The printed board tag reads 'Ans b AI 2006'.

items.stem: State the type of lens used to get; (i) Virtual and diminished image of an object. (ii) Real and diminished image of an object. Justify your answers in the above two cases by drawing ray diagrams. Which of the above lens can also form (i) real and magnified and (ii) virtual and magnified image of an object? Draw a ray diagram to justify your answer.
items.answer:
(i) Concave lens — for every position of the object it forms a virtual, erect and diminished image between the optical centre and the focus, on the same side as the object.
(ii) Convex lens — when the object is placed beyond 2F, it forms a real, inverted and diminished image between F and 2F on the other side of the lens.
A convex lens can form a real and magnified image as well as a virtual and magnified image of an object:
(i) real and magnified image — when the object is placed between F and 2F, the image is formed beyond 2F;
(ii) virtual and magnified image — when the object is placed within the focal length, the image is formed on the same side as the object.
items.ocr: No board/year tag is printed for this question. The printed answer is the bare words '(i) Concave lens.', '(ii) Convex lens.' and 'Convex lens can form a real and magnified image as well as a virtual and magnified image of an object' with four ray diagrams captioned 'Real and magnified image' and 'Virtual and magnified image'; the object positions were read from those diagrams.

items.stem: A 2.0 cm tall object is placed perpendicular to the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The distance of the object from the lens is 15 cm. Find the nature, position and size of the image formed.
items.answer:
Given, object size h = 2.0 cm, focal length of convex lens f = 10 cm, object distance u = −15 cm, image distance v = ?, image height h′ = ?
Formula, 1/v − 1/u = 1/f
1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 − 1/15 = (3 − 2)/30 = 1/30
So v = 30 cm
Magnification, m = h′/h = v/u
h′/2.0 = 30/(−15) = −2
h′ = −4.0 cm
The nature of the image is real, inverted and enlarged; it is formed at a distance of 30 cm on the right side (the other side) of the lens and is 4.0 cm in size.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode; the OCR garbles the substitution line as '1/10 − 1/15 − 1/30' — restored to = 1/30, which gives the printed v = 30 cm. Page furniture 'Click Here to Buy book on Amazon' stripped from between the question and its answer.

items.stem: A needle placed 45 cm from a lens forms an image on a screen placed 90 cm on the other side of the lens. Identify the type of lens. Determine its focal length and the power. What is the size of image, if needle is 5 cm in height?
items.answer:
Since the image formed is on the other side of the lens and can be caught on a screen (real image), the lens is a convex lens.
Here, u = −45 cm and v = 90 cm.
1/f = 1/v − 1/u = (1/90) − (−1/45) = (1 + 2)/90 = 3/90 = 1/30
f = 30 cm = 0.30 m
Power, P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.30 = +3.33 D
m = v/u = 90/(−45) = −2
m = h_i/h_o  ⇒  −2 = h_i/5  ⇒  h_i = −10 cm
So the image is real, inverted and 10 cm in height.

items.stem: (i) To construct a ray diagram we use two rays which are so chosen that it is easy to know their directions after reflection from the mirror. List two such rays and state the path of these rays after reflection in case of concave mirrors. Use these two rays and draw ray diagrams to locate the image of an object placed between pole and focus of a concave mirror. (ii) A concave mirror produces three times magnified image on a screen. If the object is placed 20 cm in front of the mirror, how far is the screen from the object.
items.answer:
(i) Two light rays whose paths after reflection are known are:
(a) The incident ray passing through the centre of curvature — after reflecting from the concave mirror the light moves back along the same path (because it strikes the mirror normally).
(b) The ray incident obliquely towards the pole of the mirror — the incident ray is reflected back by the reflecting surface of the concave mirror obliquely, making an equal angle with the principal axis.
Using these two rays, for an object placed between the focus and the pole of a concave mirror the reflected rays diverge and their backward extensions meet behind the mirror, so the image is virtual, erect and magnified.
(ii) The image is formed on a screen, so it is real and inverted: m = −3 and u = −20 cm.
m = −v/u  ⇒  −3 = −v/(−20)  ⇒  v = −60 cm
The screen is 60 cm from the mirror, so its distance from the object is 60 − 20 = 40 cm.
items.ocr: The printed material carries only part (i) — the two rays plus three ray diagrams (the third one appearing on page 50 through the column layout). No worked solution for part (ii) survives in the print/OCR, so the numerical answer (v = −60 cm, screen 40 cm from the object) was derived from the printed data.

items.stem: (i) If the image formed by a mirror for all positions of the object placed in front of it is always diminished, erect and virtual, state the type of the mirror and also draw a ray diagram to justify your answer. Write one use such mirrors are put to and why. (ii) Define the radius of curvature of spherical mirrors. Find the nature and focal length of a spherical mirror whose radius of curvature is +24 cm.
items.answer:
(i) A convex mirror forms an erect, diminished and virtual image for all the positions of the object placed in front of it. Convex mirrors are commonly used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles, as they always give an erect, though diminished, image and hence cover a much wider field of view of the traffic behind.
(ii) The radius of the sphere of which the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror forms a part is called the radius of curvature of the mirror.
Given R = +24 cm. Since the radius of curvature is positive, the mirror is a convex mirror.
f = R/2 = 24/2 = 12 cm
Thus, the focal length of the convex spherical mirror is 12 cm.

Also 'infront' expanded to 'in front'. The printed solution gives R = 24 cm and f = 24/2 = 12 cm and states the mirror is convex.
